Commentary.Commentary: We are back. The two umpires make their way out to the middle as do the players. It will be Usman Khawaja and Steven Smith to open the innings for Australia. Tim Southee will kick things off with the new ball for New Zealand. Off we go...
... THIRD INNINGS ...

A sensational bowling performance from Australia to bowl New Zealand out for 179! The visitors have taken a massive first-innings lead of 204 runs. The Aussies have decided not to enforce the follow-on and they will come out to bat again. A disappointing batting effort from the hosts has put the visitors in complete command of this Test. In reply to Australia's 383, New Zealand were off to a dreadful start. Tom Latham was the first to perish and soon it got worse for them as Kane Williamson was run out for a duck. Rachin Ravindra, Will Young and Daryl Mitchell could not do much either and the Kiwis found themselves reeling at 29-5. Glenn Phillips and Tom Blundell batted with intent after Tea but Blundell's departure left Phillips searching for partners. He found an able alley in Matt Henry and they did well to keep the runs flowing. However, Phillips fell on 71 after which Henry fought a lone fight before being dismissed on 42. Nathan Lyon was introduced late into the attack but it did not take him much long to get into the act and ended with four wickets to his name. With just over half an hour to go in the day's play, New Zealand need to make the new ball count. Can they succeed in doing so? We shall find out in a bit.

Commentary.Commentary: Drinks! New Zealand launched into the first half of this session with an electrifying display from Glenn Phillips and Tom Blundell, who exuded intent and swiftly escalated the scoring rate. Their proactive batting not only put Australia on the back foot but also injected a sense of resurgence for the Kiwis. However, Nathan Lyon's masterclass turned the tide back, claiming two wickets in an over and reshaping the narrative of this session. Matt Henry has looked good alongside Glenn Phillips taking the attack onto the bowlers and this partnership will play a crucial role for the Kiwis.

Australia, buoyed by momentum, made an impressive start to their innings, immediately asserting their dominance. The bowlers maintained disciplined lines and lengths from the outset, preventing the New Zealand batters from settling in comfortably. Mitchell Starc struck early, dismissing Tom Latham to provide the perfect start for the Aussies. The momentum continued in Australia's favour as they capitalized on an unexpected gift, claiming the wicket of Kane Williamson. Josh Hazlewood further bolstered Australia's position by joining forces, removing the left-hander Rachin Ravindra for a duck. With three quick wickets falling, Australia's bowlers continued their lethal bowling attack and put New Zealand under immense pressure. Pat Cummins emerged as a pivotal figure, breaking the resistance for the fourth wicket by setting up Daryl Mitchell brilliantly. Mitchell Marsh capitalized on the momentum, dismissing Will Young off the very next ball to send shockwaves through the Kiwi camp. The responsibility now falls on Glenn Phillips and Tom Blundell to stabilize the Kiwi innings and forge a partnership that can lift their side out of the current predicament while Australia will look to go for the kill. Stick around for an exciting final session of Day 2 which will come to you at 8:30 am IST (3 am GMT).

SESSION SUMMARY - 42 runs, 21 overs and 5 wickets. Australia has firmly grasped control of the game, exerting relentless pressure on the Kiwis and continuing to dominate proceedings winning this session. The hosts endured a challenging start to their innings post-lunch, facing even greater adversity than earlier in the day. Tom Latham was dismissed early in the innings, setting a troubling tone for New Zealand. A sudden mix-up in running between Kane Williamson and Will Young, resulted in Williamson's dismissal shortly, further compounding the pressure on the Kiwis. Rachin Ravindra, tasked with stabilizing the innings, succumbed to the mounting pressure and lost his wicket while attempting an expansive drive. The flurry of wickets saw New Zealand lose three batters in just six balls, significantly setting them back in the game. Daryl Mitchell and Will Young displayed resilience in the face of relentless pressure from the Aussie pace attack, diligently blocking balls and weathering the storm. However, their resistance was short-lived as both batters fell victim to successive deliveries after showing signs of defiance.

OUT! CAUGHT! Another one bites the dust and New Zealand are in all sorts of trouble. Josh Hazlewood comes from over the wicket and pushes this one a little wider on off on a fuller length, inviting the drive, Rachin Ravindra stays in the crease and frees his arms to drive it through covers but slices to the left of Nathan Lyon at point who moves across a bit too much to his right and gets himself into a tangle. He recovers well though to complete the catch as the ball sticks in his left hand near his armpit.

OUT! RUN OUT! Oh dear, that's a terrible mixup and Kane Williamson has to walk back without troubling the scorers. Mitchell Starc gets this nice and full, around off, Kane Williamson covers the line, taps it in front of mid off and sets off for the run. Will Young is caught ball-watching and then turns back to run but crashes right into Kane Williamson as Starc holds his ground in the middle of the two batters. Marnus Labuschagne at mid off collects the ball and hits the stumps at the bowler's end to catch Williamson well short of his crease.
